clue.text: Single forehand shot and scores are settled

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken up, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A tennis player wins a point with one forehand and squares an old grudge with an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like the tennis stroke the forehand makes, but it is the anagram signal for SINGLE FOREHAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying there are no hard feelings declares that any grudge has been dropped, like old scores being settled.

clue.text: Projection, which could produce a headache with part exchange

indicators.note: the two parts of the word swap places, the front section moving to the back, like trading in an old car

parts.note: a hangover is the headache after a night's drinking

explanation.surface: A projection that, traded in with part exchange, would leave you with a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part exchange' is the British term for trading in an old item against a new one; here HANG and OVER swap ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhang is a part of a structure or rock that juts out, a projection.

clue.text: Dual Asian model somewhere in southern Europe …

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so these letters are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: An Asian model with two nationalities turns up somewhere on the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a person posing, but it is a verb telling you to reshape DUAL ASIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is the autonomous region of southern Spain, a vague but accurate location in southern Europe.

clue.text: … lowers self for Europeans — just saying!

indicators.note: the phrase means only spoken, so the word for these Europeans is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Danes, the people of Denmark, are Europeans

explanation.surface: Following on from the last clue, someone condescends to Europeans and shrugs it off as a passing remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clue to 3 down but adds nothing to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, to stoop to doing something beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: See 1
Film of float at a tantric gathering

indicators.note: gathering means collecting things together into a heap, so these letters are pooled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drifts about at a gathering devoted to tantric practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' looks like a meeting where the floating happens, but it signals the anagram of FLOAT AT A TANTRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal Attraction is the 1987 thriller starring Michael Douglas and Glenn Close.

clue.text: What about cunning bloke? He's no alien

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for what goes around the next piece

parts.note: eh is an interjection asking what, as in 'Eh? What did you say?'
art can mean craft or cunning, as in artful
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: Someone asks, puzzled, about a crafty fellow who turns out to be no alien.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction an Earthman is a human from Earth, the opposite of an alien visitor.

clue.text: See 12
Past one's best, left to admit defeat on the radio

parts.note: someone who has left has gone

indicators.note: words broadcast on the radio are heard, not seen, so this phrase is taken by sound

parts.note: to cede is to give way or concede defeat

explanation.surface: A washed-up figure leaves, conceding defeat in a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant gone to seed has stopped flowering; idiomatically a person gone to seed has declined in looks or vigour.

clue.text: This forced one to take the stairs, thus getting exercise

definitions.text: This forced one to take the stairs
definitions.meaning: a broken-down elevator, which leaves you walking up
the ... is a weightlifting exercise, raising a barbell from the floor

explanation.surface: A broken lift made someone climb the stairs, so they got a workout anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as DEAD LIFT, a lift that has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlift is a gym lift of a loaded bar from the ground to hip height.

clue.text: Cycling in Yorkshire?

definitions.meaning: the ... were the three historic divisions of Yorkshire, an English county: North, East and West

explanation.surface: A question about bike rides in Yorkshire, host of the Tour de France start in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding is the act of travelling on a bicycle, and also a historic administrative district of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Singletons?

parts.note: single people looking for partners, as in newspaper personal columns

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singletons' could mean single items or only children; the question mark points to unattached people seeking love.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely hearts are single people seeking romance, often through dating advertisements.

clue.text: A father's wise rewriting of an idiot's novel

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, and the possessive gives PA'S
sage means wise

indicators.note: rewriting means writing the letters out again in a new order

parts.note: the word idiot, its possessive linking the fodder to the definition

explanation.surface: A wise father rewrites a novel written by a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting of' rearranges AN IDIOT into TO INDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Passage to India is E. M. Forster's 1924 novel about British India.

clue.text: Resorts of times past

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the answer is a part of the following words

explanation.surface: Resorts that belong to bygone days, like old Victorian spa towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Spas are resorts built around mineral springs, visited for health cures.

clue.text: Monk sounds drunk on gin

indicators.note: on means placed after, the drunk part coming after the gin part

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

indicators.note: sounds means the word for drunk is said, not spelt

parts.note: pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A monk sounds as though he has had too much gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink, fitting the drunk monk, but it is a trap for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappists are Cistercian monks of the strict observance, famous for brewing beer.

clue.text: Nice person demonstrated a little energy

parts.note: something demonstrated has been proven
cal is short for calorie, a small unit of energy

explanation.surface: A pleasant person showed a little vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective meaning pleasant, but it is the French city, so a Nice person comes from Provence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice is a city in Provence, so its inhabitant is a Provençal, a native of that region.

clue.text: 2% of Hawaii, as a state

definitions.meaning: two per cent is one part in fifty
Hawaii was the ... state admitted to the United States, in 1959

explanation.surface: Hawaii makes up two per cent of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiftieth is the fraction one over fifty, and the ordinal for the last state to join the union.

clue.text: Mushy peas served with pork pie, right for trainer

indicators.note: mushy means mashed to a pulp, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie

explanation.surface: A British pub meal of mushy peas and pork pie, with something fitting for a trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas; 'Mushy' rearranges PEAS into ESPA.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a lattice or frame on which fruit trees are trained flat against a wall.

clue.text: 15's range

indicators.note: the possessive says the answer is something belonging to the word at 15, a part held within it

parts.note: the answer to 15 down, the word for a person from Nice

explanation.surface: A cooker that belongs to the person from Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on 15 is the only signal: strip PR and CAL from the ends of PROVENCAL and the cooker is left inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen cooker, which includes an oven.

clue.text: After a short time, moved up and down

indicators.note: after means the moved-up word follows the short time in the answer

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a short time
rose means moved up

explanation.surface: After a little while, something went up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' reads as a pair, but 'moved up' gives ROSE and 'down' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Down means low in spirits, which is the same as morose, sullen and gloomy.

clue.text: Attractive European's bearing?

parts.note: magnetic means attractive, literally and figuratively
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A question about the posture of a charming European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like a person's manner, but it is a compass bearing taken from a magnetic pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass bearings are taken relative to magnetic north, so a magnetic pole is the reference for a bearing.

clue.text: Special position of hotel in 15 location

indicators.note: in means the hotel letter sits within the city's name

parts.note: Nice is a city in Provence, the region of 15 down
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel's special position in a Provençal town.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a specialised position or role that suits someone, as in finding one's niche.

clue.text: See 2
Make secure?

indicators.note: to make something from these letters is to build a new word from them

explanation.surface: A query about how to make something safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works twice: rearrange SECURE, and to rescue is to make safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them from danger, putting them in safety.

clue.text: Inflexible, as if in Fife

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for the metal, and in the word Fife those two letters wrap around the little word if, as the clue's 'if in' points out

explanation.surface: Someone stiff and unbending, as though they lived in Fife.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: Fe is iron, and in FIFE it is clad around IF. Fife is a council area in eastern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironclad means unbreakable or rigid, as in an ironclad guarantee.

clue.text: Their own pants became threadbare

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a bad version to be reordered

explanation.surface: Their own trousers wore out with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like the trousers, but it signals the anagram of THEIR OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that wore thin was worn down until it was threadbare.

clue.text: Stick around, admitting love by the end of fiery speech

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the zero goes inside
around means turned round, so the word for stick is read backwards

parts.note: glue means stick
love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone sticks with a fiery speech that ends in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns GLUE into EULG, and 'admitting' puts O inside it to give EULOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech praising someone, especially at a funeral.
